steps.say: Silent gallstones need no treatment, with under two percent yearly biliary pain risk. Wall thickening over three millimetres and a positive Murphy sign mark acute cholecystitis, not simple biliary colic. Learn to separate colic pain from true inflammation.
steps.tx: Asymptomatic gallstones need no treatment with under **2** percent yearly biliary pain risk, while acute **cholecystitis** shows **wall thickening** over **3** mm and a **Murphy sign**, unlike simple biliary colic. Colic pain settles within hours without fever or white cells, while cholecystitis brings fever, tachycardia and a tender palpable gallbladder. Ultrasound wall, stone impaction and pericholecystic fluid confirm the inflamed diagnosis.

steps.say: Tokyo grading sorts cholecystitis into mild localised, moderate with a palpable mass or symptoms beyond seventy two hours, and severe with organ dysfunction. Grade decides between early surgery and drainage. Grading happens at presentation, not after days of dithering.
steps.tx: **Tokyo grading** sorts cholecystitis as mild localised, moderate with palpable mass or symptom duration over **72** hours, and severe with **organ dysfunction**, deciding between early surgery and drainage. Moderate disease in fit patients still goes to early laparoscopy, while severe grade with hypotension or confusion needs resuscitation plus drainage first. Re-grade daily, since moderate disease can tip into organ failure overnight.

steps.say: Operating within seventy two hours of cholecystitis onset beats delayed surgery for complications and hospital stay. The critical view of safety exposing exactly two structures entering the gallbladder prevents catastrophic bile duct injury. Never clip what you cannot see entering the gallbladder.
steps.tx: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within **72** hours of cholecystitis onset beats delayed surgery for complications and stay, with **critical view of safety** exposing two structures entering the gallbladder. The hepatocystic triangle cleared of fat, the lower third off the cystic plate and only cystic duct plus artery seen define the view. Photograph it, and convert or bail to subtotal cholecystectomy when inflammation hides the anatomy.

vis.alt: Critical view of safety with hepatocystic triangle cleared, cystic plate exposed, cystic artery and duct seen entering the gallbladder.
vis.caption: Critical view of safety dissection. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Common duct stones with cholangitis, jaundice or a duct dilated over six millimetres need preoperative ERCP clearance. Fit patients with large stones suit single stage laparoscopic bile duct exploration instead. Clear the duct before or during cholecystectomy whenever possible; a stone left behind means a second procedure.
steps.tx: Common bile duct stones with cholangitis, jaundice or dilated duct over **6** mm need preoperative **ERCP clearance**, while single-stage laparoscopic **bile duct exploration** suits fit patients with large stones. Sphincterotomy with balloon sweep clears most stones, and failed ERCP redirects to exploration or rendezvous procedures. Image the duct in every cholecystitis with raised liver enzymes, since silent stones cause retained-stone sepsis.

steps.say: Mirizzi compresses the common hepatic duct from an impacted cystic duct stone. Csendes types one to five run from simple compression (one), through cholecystobiliary fistula of growing size (two to four), to cholecystoenteric fistula (five). Larger duct defects need hepaticojejunostomy. Suspect it when jaundice accompanies cholecystitis with a shrunken gallbladder.
steps.tx: **Mirizzi** syndrome compresses the common hepatic duct from an impacted cystic duct stone, classified Csendes **I** to **V**: **I** is external compression, **II** to **IV** are cholecystobiliary fistula of increasing duct erosion, and **V** is cholecystoenteric fistula. Type **I** needs subtotal or total cholecystectomy, small type **II** fistulas can be closed over a gallbladder remnant, and larger fistulas (**III** and **IV**) need hepaticojejunostomy. Preoperative MRCP maps the level, since unrecognised Mirizzi turns routine cholecystectomy into bile duct injury.

vis.alt: Impacted Hartmann pouch stone compressing the common hepatic duct with Csendes type I compression and types II to IV fistula diagrams.
vis.caption: Mirizzi compression with Csendes fistula types. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Bouveret blocks the gastric outlet with a giant gallstone that fistulised into the duodenum. Stones over two and a half centimetres need enterolithotomy first, with cholecystectomy deferred to a second stage. Vomiting elderly patients with pneumobilia carry this diagnosis until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: **Bouveret** syndrome with gastric outlet obstruction from a cholecystoduodenal (biliary-enteric) fistula stone over **2.5** cm needs **enterolithotomy** first, with cholecystectomy deferred to a second stage. Rigler features of obstruction plus pneumobilia with an ectopic shadow clinch it, and endoscopic retrieval fails for stones this large. Milk the stone to healthy jejunum before opening bowel, since duodenal oedema leaks if closed under tension.

vis.alt: Biliary enteric fistula with a large gallstone impacted at the pyloric channel causing gastric outlet obstruction.
vis.caption: Bouveret outlet block from fistula stone. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Gallbladder polyps over ten millimetres, sessile shape or primary sclerosing cholangitis background need cholecystectomy for cancer risk. Small pedunculated polyps in a normal gallbladder stay under ultrasound watch. Never ignore a polyp in a sclerosing cholangitis liver.
steps.tx: **Gallbladder polyp** over **10** mm, **sessile** morphology or primary sclerosing cholangitis background needs cholecystectomy because of malignant potential. Cholesterol polyps under 10 mm without risk factors get yearly ultrasound, and growth or vascularity on review triggers surgery. Indian ethnicity, age over 50 and solitary polyps each raise the stakes toward earlier removal.

steps.say: Percutaneous cholecystostomy bridges severe cholecystitis in unfit patients who cannot survive surgery. Interval cholecystectomy at six to eight weeks follows once sepsis resolves and fitness improves. The drain buys time, not cure.
steps.tx: Percutaneous **cholecystostomy** bridges severe cholecystitis in unfit patients, with **interval cholecystectomy** at **6** to **8** weeks once sepsis resolves and fitness improves. Ultrasound-guided transhepatic drain decompresses the empyema within hours, and a tube cholangiogram later maps stones and Mirizzi. Persistent fistula output or recurrent attacks after recovery still end in delayed surgery.
